# WebsiteSoft

> WebsiteSoft is a web and software development company, working since 2007. We build, upgrade and migrate Umbraco, Sitecore (including SitecoreAI) and Optimizely websites, develop custom .NET software and integrations, and add practical AI to existing systems. Contact: enquiries@websitesoft.co.uk.

Key facts:
- Founded: 2007
- Platforms: Umbraco, Sitecore, SitecoreAI, Optimizely CMS, .NET
- Services: CMS development and migration, upgrades and support, custom .NET applications, APIs and integration, legacy modernisation, AI integration, AI search, document automation, AI website QA testing
- Every change is peer-reviewed before release; we write our own code with few dependencies
- Email: enquiries@websitesoft.co.uk

## AI Integration & AI-Powered Solutions
- [AI Integration & AI-Powered Solutions](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/ai/): We add AI to the applications and websites you already run, securely and with people in control.
  AI integration at WebsiteSoft adds AI to existing applications and websites, securely and with people in control. Services include assistants grounded in approved content, semantic search across websites and documents, document processing and workflow automation, and an AI QA testing tool in development, through a secure .NET layer to Azure OpenAI and other providers.
  - Q: Do we need to rebuild our systems to add AI? A: No. WebsiteSoft adds a secure .NET layer between existing systems and AI services such as Azure OpenAI, so the current website, CMS or application stays in place and gains the new capability without a replacement project.
  - Q: How do you stop an AI assistant giving wrong answers? A: By grounding it in approved content only, returning sources with answers, and routing uncertain cases to people. Accuracy, safety and cost are tested before launch and monitored afterwards, so quality is measured rather than assumed.
  - Q: Is our data kept secure when using AI? A: The design decides which data the AI can see and which it cannot, access goes through a controlled .NET layer, and humans review outputs where needed. Which provider and hosting region is appropriate depends on your data requirements.
- [AI integration and smart assistants](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/ai/ai-integration/): Add AI to your existing website, CMS or application, including assistants that answer from your own approved content.
  AI integration and assistants at WebsiteSoft add AI to an existing website, CMS or application through a secure .NET layer to Azure OpenAI. Capabilities include drafting, summarising and tagging, and assistants that answer only from approved content, with human review and cost monitoring, so businesses gain AI without replacing systems and keep data under control.
  - Q: What can an AI assistant grounded in our content do? A: It answers customer and staff questions using only the content you have approved, such as product information, policies or help articles, and declines or escalates when the answer is not there. This avoids the invented answers generic chatbots give.
  - Q: How do you control the cost of AI features? A: Usage is monitored from the start, with limits and alerts, and use cases are chosen where AI saves clear effort. Testing before launch covers cost alongside accuracy and safety, so running costs are understood before rollout.
  - Q: Which AI providers do you work with? A: Azure OpenAI is the usual starting point for organisations already on Microsoft, and the .NET layer can connect to other providers. The choice depends on data residency, existing contracts and the specific use case.
- [AI-powered search](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/ai/ai-search/): Search that understands meaning and intent across your website, documents and knowledge base.
  AI-powered search from WebsiteSoft understands meaning and intent across a website, documents and knowledge base using semantic and vector search. Results can include answers grounded in your own content with sources shown, and it works with Umbraco, Sitecore and Optimizely. Visitors find what they need, support enquiries fall and analytics show what people look for.
  - Q: How is AI search different from the keyword search we have? A: Keyword search matches the words typed. Semantic and vector search matches the meaning, so a question phrased differently from the page still finds it. Answers can also be generated from the matching content, with sources shown.
  - Q: Can AI search work with our existing CMS? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft indexes content from Umbraco, Sitecore and Optimizely sites, and can include documents and knowledge bases alongside web pages. The content stays in the CMS; the search index is built from it and kept updated.
  - Q: How do you make sure search results are accurate? A: Search is tuned with real queries from your users before launch, and search analytics afterwards show what people look for and where results fall short. Generated answers cite their sources so users can check them.
- [Document processing and workflow automation](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/ai/document-automation/): Read, extract and route information from documents automatically, and automate repetitive process steps.
  Document processing and workflow automation from WebsiteSoft reads, extracts and routes information from invoices, forms and contracts, and automates repetitive process steps. The work covers data extraction, classification and routing, Power Automate and custom .NET workflows, with people reviewing anything uncertain. Organisations remove manual retyping, cut errors and backlogs and gain clear audit trails.
  - Q: What types of documents can be processed automatically? A: Typically invoices, forms and contracts, in scanned or digital form. Suitability is checked by reviewing real samples at the start, as layout variety and image quality affect extraction accuracy more than the document type itself.
  - Q: What happens when the system is not sure about a document? A: It is routed to a person for review rather than guessed. Confidence thresholds are set during testing on real cases, so the system handles the routine majority and people handle the exceptions, with an audit trail of both.
  - Q: Do you use Power Automate or custom code? A: Both, depending on the process. Power Automate suits organisations on Microsoft 365 with straightforward routing needs. Custom .NET workflows are used where logic is complex, volumes are high or integration goes beyond what Power Automate offers.

## Custom Software Development
- [Custom Software Development](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/custom-software/): When off-the-shelf tools do not fit, we build .NET applications, web apps, APIs and integrations around how your business works.
  Custom software development at WebsiteSoft covers .NET applications, portals, APIs and integrations built around how a business works when off-the-shelf tools do not fit. WebsiteSoft has traded since 2007 and builds in C# and .NET with minimal dependencies, giving software that fits the business, fewer security risks and code any team can maintain.
  - Q: What drives the cost of custom software? A: Mainly the number of processes and user roles covered, the systems it must integrate with and how much data needs migrating. WebsiteSoft prototypes first and plans releases, so the first version can be scoped to the parts that matter most.
  - Q: Will we be tied to WebsiteSoft to maintain the software? A: No. Applications are built with clean architecture, minimal dependencies and documentation, so any competent .NET team can pick them up. Many clients keep WebsiteSoft on for support, but the code is written so that remains a choice.
  - Q: Can you replace our spreadsheets with a proper application? A: Yes, this is a common starting point. WebsiteSoft talks to the people doing the work, reviews the spreadsheets and processes, then prototypes an application before the full build so the fit is confirmed early.
- [APIs and enterprise integration](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/custom-software/api-integrations/): Secure APIs and integrations that connect your CRM, ERP, finance and other systems, so data is entered once.
  API and enterprise integration at WebsiteSoft connects CRM, ERP, finance and other systems so data is entered once and shared automatically. The work covers documented REST and GraphQL APIs, retries, monitoring and alerts, and clear data ownership rules, giving one consistent view of the business, manual retyping removed and new systems added without rework.
  - Q: Can you integrate systems that have poor or no documentation? A: Usually, yes. WebsiteSoft reviews what each system exposes and the quality of its data before designing flows. Where an API is missing or weak, options include database-level access, file exchange or wrapping the system in a documented API.
  - Q: What happens when one system is down? A: The integration layer is designed for failure. Messages are retried, errors are logged and alerts are raised, so data is delivered when the system returns rather than lost. Failure handling is tested deliberately before deployment.
  - Q: Who decides which system holds the master data? A: That is agreed at the start as data ownership rules: for each type of data, one system is the source of truth and the others receive updates from it. This prevents conflicting records and makes later changes predictable.
- [.NET and web applications](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/custom-software/dotnet-applications/): Business applications, portals and internal tools in C# and modern .NET, replacing spreadsheets and manual steps.
  .NET and web application development at WebsiteSoft produces business applications, portals and dashboards in C# and modern .NET, replacing spreadsheets and manual steps. Applications use clean architecture with minimal dependencies and secure sign-in with roles, and are prototyped before the full build, giving software that fits the business and code any team can pick up.
  - Q: How long does a custom .NET application take to build? A: It depends on scope. WebsiteSoft builds in short iterations and plans releases, so a first working version typically arrives early and grows from there, rather than everything landing at the end of a long project.
  - Q: Why avoid dependency-heavy code? A: Every third-party package is something that can break on update, go unmaintained or carry a vulnerability. Keeping dependencies minimal and the architecture clean means updates are smaller, security risk is lower and the code stays understandable.
  - Q: How do you make sure the software fits how we work? A: By talking to the people who do the work, reviewing the current tools, data and processes, and building a prototype before the full build. Testing uses real scenarios from the business rather than invented ones.
- [Legacy system modernisation](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/custom-software/legacy-modernisation/): Modernise old applications in stages, moving to modern .NET and the cloud without stopping the business.
  Legacy system modernisation at WebsiteSoft moves old applications to modern .NET and the cloud in stages without stopping the business. It documents how the system behaves, replaces it module by module, migrates .NET Framework code to modern .NET and moves hosting to Azure, giving lower risk than a rewrite, a supported platform and faster changes.
  - Q: Is it better to modernise or rewrite from scratch? A: Staged modernisation is typically lower risk. A rewrite delivers nothing until it is finished and often misses undocumented behaviour. Module-by-module replacement delivers value early, tests each part against the existing system and keeps the business running.
  - Q: Can you modernise a system when the original developers have left? A: Yes. The first step is documenting how the system actually works, from the code, the data and the people who use it every day. That documentation then becomes the test baseline for each modernised module.
  - Q: Do we have to move to the cloud as part of modernisation? A: No. Cloud migration to Azure is one option within the staged plan, not a requirement. Some systems move hosting first, others modernise code first, depending on what must keep running and where the biggest risk sits.

## Optimizely Development
- [Optimizely Development](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/optimizely/): We build, customise, integrate and upgrade websites on Optimizely CMS (formerly Episerver), including upgrades to CMS 13.
  Optimizely development at WebsiteSoft covers building, customising, integrating and upgrading websites on Optimizely CMS, formerly Episerver, including upgrades from CMS 11 or 12 to Optimizely CMS 13 on .NET 10. Sites are set up around how editors work, connected to CRM, ERP, PIM and marketing systems, and kept on the current release with rankings protected.
  - Q: Is Optimizely CMS the same as Episerver? A: Yes. Episerver was renamed Optimizely, and Episerver CMS 11 is the version many sites still run. Optimizely CMS 12 and CMS 13 are its successors, with CMS 13 reaching general availability on 31 March 2026 on .NET 10.
  - Q: Can you take over an existing Optimizely site? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft reviews the existing site, content model and add-ons first, then agrees what to improve, integrate or upgrade. Most work builds on the current solution rather than replacing it, unless the version is too far behind.
  - Q: What does an Optimizely project typically start with? A: A discussion of goals, audiences and editor workflow, followed by a review of the current site, content and integrations. From that WebsiteSoft designs the content model, components and roles before building in iterations.
- [Optimizely development and implementation](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/optimizely/optimizely-development/): New Optimizely sites and custom features, set up around how your editors work, with roles and approvals.
  Optimizely development and implementation at WebsiteSoft covers new Optimizely CMS sites and custom features built on supported extension points, set up around how editors work. The work includes a content model and component library, roles, access rights and approvals, and editor training. Editors run the site confidently, publishing is safe and change costs are lower.
  - Q: Why do custom Optimizely features break during upgrades? A: Usually because they were built with workarounds rather than on Optimizely's supported extension points. WebsiteSoft builds customisations against the documented APIs so they typically carry through CMS upgrades with little or no rework.
  - Q: Can you set up approvals so mistakes do not go live? A: Yes. Optimizely CMS supports roles, access rights and approval sequences. WebsiteSoft configures these around your editor workflow so content is reviewed before publishing, and documents the setup in editor guides for new starters.
  - Q: How do you decide the page and block types? A: By looking at the content editors actually publish and the layouts the site needs, then designing a small, consistent set of page and block types. Confusing or overlapping types are the main cause of slow editing.
- [Optimizely integrations](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/optimizely/optimizely-integrations/): Connect Optimizely to your CRM, ERP, PIM, marketing and analytics systems through secure APIs.
  Optimizely integration at WebsiteSoft connects Optimizely CMS to CRM, ERP, PIM, marketing automation and analytics systems through secure APIs built in .NET. The work covers CRM and marketing automation, PIM and ERP data sync, single sign-on and content APIs for apps and other channels, so sites show accurate data, manual transfer stops and personalisation improves.
  - Q: Which systems can you connect to Optimizely? A: Typically CRM, marketing automation, PIM, ERP and analytics platforms, plus identity providers for single sign-on. Any system with a usable API can be considered; WebsiteSoft reviews the APIs and data quality before designing the flows.
  - Q: How do you handle failures in an integration? A: Each flow is designed with retries, logging and alerts, and tested with real data and deliberate failures before go-live. Deployment includes monitoring so problems are visible rather than silently leaving stale data on the site.
  - Q: Can Optimizely content be used in our mobile app? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft builds content APIs so content managed in Optimizely can be delivered to apps and other channels. On Optimizely CMS 13, Optimizely Graph is a required part of the platform and the standard route for content delivery.
- [Optimizely upgrades and migration](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/optimizely/optimizely-migration/): Upgrade Episerver CMS 11 or Optimizely CMS 12 to CMS 13 on .NET 10, including the move to Optimizely Graph.
  An Optimizely upgrade moves Episerver CMS 11 or CMS 12 to Optimizely CMS 13, which runs on .NET 10 and requires Optimizely Graph and Opti ID. WebsiteSoft inventories code and add-ons, upgrades the solution, moves search and content delivery to Optimizely Graph, replaces unsupported add-ons and adds redirects, leaving the supported CMS with rankings protected.
  - Q: What changes between Optimizely CMS 12 and CMS 13? A: CMS 13 reached general availability on 31 March 2026 and runs on .NET 10. Optimizely Graph and Opti ID are required parts of it, so search, content delivery and sign-in typically need changes even when the content model stays the same.
  - Q: Can we upgrade straight from Episerver CMS 11 to CMS 13? A: The path depends on the solution and its add-ons. CMS 11 is two major releases behind CMS 13, so WebsiteSoft reviews the code and add-ons first, then chooses between a direct migration and staged phases with regression testing at each step.
  - Q: What happens to our add-ons during the upgrade? A: Each add-on is reviewed for a CMS 13-compatible version. Those without one are replaced with supported alternatives or custom code on documented extension points. Search add-ons typically move to Optimizely Graph as part of the upgrade.

## Sitecore Development & Migration
- [Sitecore Development & Migration](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/sitecore/): We support and upgrade Sitecore XP and XM, build and integrate features, and move businesses to SitecoreAI when the time is right.
  Sitecore development at WebsiteSoft covers support and upgrades for Sitecore XP and XM, building components, templates, workflows and integrations, and migration to SitecoreAI, the SaaS platform formerly called XM Cloud, when the time is right. Sites stay supported and secure, editors work independently, and organisations get advice on upgrading, moving to SitecoreAI or changing platform.
  - Q: Do you support older Sitecore XP versions? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft keeps legacy Sitecore versions stable and hardened while the next step is planned, fixing blockers and applying security measures. Which versions remain practical to support depends on the modules and custom code in the installation.
  - Q: Is SitecoreAI the same as XM Cloud? A: Yes. Sitecore renamed XM Cloud to SitecoreAI in November 2025. It is Sitecore's SaaS platform with a headless front end, so moving to it from XP or XM is a migration project rather than a version upgrade.
  - Q: Can you work alongside our in-house Sitecore team? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft typically fills gaps in specialist skills, reviews code and handles upgrades or integrations while the in-house team keeps day-to-day ownership. Work is documented and code-reviewed so knowledge does not sit with one person.
- [Sitecore development and integrations](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/sitecore/sitecore-development/): Components, templates and workflows built properly, plus integrations with your CRM, DAM and business systems.
  Sitecore development and integration at WebsiteSoft covers templates, standard values and reusable components, roles, workflows and approvals, SXA and headless development, and integrations with CRM, DAM and Microsoft Teams. Work is code-reviewed and tested for publishing and data flows, so editors add pages independently, pages stay consistent and data stays in sync across systems.
  - Q: Can you fix a messy Sitecore content tree? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft reviews the existing templates and content structure, then redesigns templates, standard values and components so new pages are quick to create. Content is restructured in stages so editors can keep publishing during the work.
  - Q: Do you work with SXA and headless Sitecore? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft builds with SXA on Sitecore XP and XM and develops headless components for SitecoreAI. The right approach depends on the current platform and whether a move to SitecoreAI is planned in the near future.
  - Q: Which systems can Sitecore be integrated with? A: Typically CRM platforms, digital asset management systems and Microsoft Teams, along with other business systems that expose an API. The integration design covers data ownership, security and failure handling before any code is written.
- [Sitecore upgrades and support](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/sitecore/sitecore-upgrades/): Upgrade older Sitecore versions safely, or keep legacy versions stable and secure while you plan the next step.
  Sitecore upgrades and support from WebsiteSoft cover upgrading older Sitecore XP and XM versions safely, and keeping legacy versions stable and secure while the next step is planned. The work includes upgrade path planning, blocker fixes, database and content upgrade, hardening and regression testing, with honest advice on upgrading, moving to SitecoreAI or an alternative.
  - Q: What usually blocks a Sitecore upgrade? A: Most often third-party modules that have no compatible release, custom pipelines or processors that depend on changed APIs, and old database schemas. WebsiteSoft reviews the install, modules and code first so blockers are fixed before the upgrade starts.
  - Q: Should we upgrade Sitecore or move to SitecoreAI? A: It depends on your licence position, the features in use and how much custom server-side code exists. WebsiteSoft sets out the costs and risks of each path, including moving to another platform, rather than recommending one by default.
  - Q: Can you keep an unsupported Sitecore version running safely? A: For a period, yes. Hardening, monitoring and targeted fixes reduce risk while a longer-term plan is agreed. It is a bridge rather than a destination, because unsupported versions no longer receive security fixes from Sitecore.
- [SitecoreAI migration](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/sitecore/sitecoreai-migration/): Move from Sitecore XP or XM to SitecoreAI (formerly XM Cloud), Sitecore's SaaS platform, in planned phases.
  A SitecoreAI migration moves a Sitecore XP or XM solution to SitecoreAI, formerly XM Cloud, in phases. WebsiteSoft assesses readiness, builds a headless front end in Next.js, migrates and tidies templates and content, and moves custom server-side logic to APIs and services. The result is no more major version upgrades and less infrastructure to manage.
  - Q: Do our existing MVC renderings carry over to SitecoreAI? A: No. SitecoreAI uses a headless front end, so MVC renderings are rebuilt as components, typically in Next.js. Custom server-side code also needs a new home in APIs or services, which is why the readiness assessment comes first.
  - Q: How long does a SitecoreAI migration take? A: It depends on the number of templates, the amount of custom code and the state of the content. WebsiteSoft runs the move in phases, so parts of the site can go live on SitecoreAI while others remain on the current platform.
  - Q: Does our content need cleaning up before moving to SitecoreAI? A: Usually, yes. Unused templates, duplicated items and stale content add cost to the migration and clutter the new platform. The review stage identifies what is actually used, and content is tidied as it moves.

## Umbraco Development & Migration
- [Umbraco Development & Migration](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/umbraco/): We build, upgrade and support Umbraco sites, and move businesses onto Umbraco from Sitecore, WordPress and other platforms.
  Umbraco development at WebsiteSoft covers building new Umbraco sites, upgrading older versions such as Umbraco 7, 8 and 13 to Umbraco 17 LTS on .NET 10, and migrating businesses onto Umbraco from Sitecore, WordPress and other platforms. Content, integrations and search rankings are carried over, and ongoing support keeps the site patched and improving.
  - Q: Which version of Umbraco should we be on? A: Umbraco 17 is the current long-term support release, running on .NET 10. Sites still on Umbraco 7, 8 or 13 should plan a move, because Umbraco 13 reaches end of life on 14 December 2026 and earlier versions are already unsupported.
  - Q: Can you take over an Umbraco site another agency built? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft starts with a review of the code, packages, hosting and version, then agrees a support plan. Most handovers need no rebuild; the review simply shows what needs patching, fixing or planning for the next upgrade.
  - Q: Will moving to Umbraco affect our search rankings? A: It should not if the move is planned. Every changed URL gets a redirect, metadata is carried across, and the new site is compared against the old before cut-over. Rankings typically hold when redirects are complete and tested.
- [WordPress and other CMS to Umbraco](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/umbraco/cms-to-umbraco-migration/): Move from WordPress, Drupal, Kentico Xperience or a bespoke CMS to a structured, secure Umbraco site.
  A CMS to Umbraco migration moves a website from WordPress, Drupal, Kentico Xperience or a bespoke CMS onto Umbraco. WebsiteSoft maps the content model to Umbraco document types, writes scripted, repeatable migration tooling, replaces plugins with maintained features and builds a redirect map for every changed URL, giving structured content, less maintenance and protected rankings.
  - Q: Will our WordPress plugins work on Umbraco? A: No, WordPress plugins cannot be installed on Umbraco. WebsiteSoft reviews what each plugin does and replaces it with an Umbraco package, a built-in feature or custom code, so the function is kept while the constant plugin updating stops.
  - Q: How is content moved from the old CMS? A: Content is exported from the old database or API and loaded into Umbraco by scripts, so the migration can be rerun as content changes before go-live. Editors check the results rather than re-entering pages manually.
  - Q: What happens to our URLs and SEO? A: Every URL that changes gets a permanent redirect in a full redirect map, and page titles, metadata and images are carried over. Links and redirects are tested before go-live, which typically keeps rankings stable through the move.
- [Sitecore to Umbraco migration](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/umbraco/sitecore-to-umbraco-migration/): Move from Sitecore to Umbraco to cut licence costs and complexity, keeping content, integrations and rankings.
  A Sitecore to Umbraco migration replaces Sitecore XP or XM with Umbraco to cut licence costs while keeping content, integrations and rankings. WebsiteSoft audits templates, renderings, workflows and modules, maps Sitecore templates to Umbraco document types, migrates content, media and languages, and moves or rebuilds .NET integrations, leaving a simpler platform with lower running costs.
  - Q: Why move from Sitecore to Umbraco rather than upgrade Sitecore? A: Many organisations pay for Sitecore features they no longer use, and a Sitecore upgrade or SitecoreAI move is a large project in itself. If the features in use map to Umbraco, the migration takes similar effort but removes the licence fee.
  - Q: Can our existing Sitecore integrations and .NET code be reused? A: Often, yes. Both platforms run on .NET, so business logic and integration code can typically be moved with changes rather than rewritten. Sitecore-specific APIs, renderings and pipelines are the parts that need rebuilding for Umbraco.
  - Q: When should we start planning a Sitecore to Umbraco migration? A: Ideally well before the Sitecore licence renewal date, as that fixes the deadline. WebsiteSoft starts by reviewing which Sitecore features are actually used and what the renewal costs, then sets a plan that lands before the renewal falls due.
- [Umbraco development and integrations](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/umbraco/umbraco-development/): New Umbraco sites, custom features and connections to your CRM, ERP and business systems.
  Umbraco development and integration at WebsiteSoft covers new Umbraco sites, custom backoffice features and connections to CRM, ERP and marketing systems through APIs. Work starts with a content model and reusable components, with headless or traditional front ends as needed. Editors publish without tickets, data flows between systems automatically and new features are delivered faster.
  - Q: Can you integrate Umbraco with our CRM or ERP? A: Yes. WebsiteSoft connects Umbraco to CRM, ERP and marketing platforms through their APIs, with the data flows and security designed first. Which systems can connect depends on the APIs they expose, which is reviewed at the start.
  - Q: Should we build a headless or traditional Umbraco site? A: It depends on where content needs to appear. A traditional Umbraco site is simpler if the website is the only channel. Headless suits apps, multiple front ends or a separate front-end framework, and WebsiteSoft builds either.
  - Q: How do you approach a new Umbraco build? A: After agreeing goals, audience and editor needs, WebsiteSoft designs the content model and integrations, then builds in short iterations so editors can test features and data flows early. Launch is followed by training and ongoing improvement.
- [Umbraco maintenance and support](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/umbraco/umbraco-support/): Keep your Umbraco site secure, up to date and improving, with a team that knows your code.
  Umbraco maintenance and support from WebsiteSoft keeps an Umbraco site secure, up to date and improving, covering updates and security patches, uptime and error monitoring, fixes and small improvements, and planning for the next upgrade. Every change is peer-reviewed, so site owners get quick fixes from a team that knows the code and predictable upgrades.
  - Q: Do you support Umbraco sites you did not build? A: Yes. Support starts with a review of the code, hosting and versions to understand how critical the site is and what needs attention first. From that review WebsiteSoft agrees a support plan rather than assuming a rebuild.
  - Q: What does an Umbraco support plan include? A: Typically regular Umbraco and package updates, security patches, uptime and error monitoring, bug fixes and small improvements, plus planning for the next major upgrade. The level of cover depends on how critical the site is to the business.
  - Q: How quickly are issues fixed? A: Response depends on the agreed support plan and the severity of the issue. Because the team already knows the code and hosting, diagnosis is usually faster than with an unfamiliar site, and every fix is peer-reviewed before release.
- [Umbraco upgrades](https://www.websitesoft.co.uk/services/umbraco/umbraco-upgrades/): Move from Umbraco 7, 8 or 13 (end of life December 2026) to Umbraco 17 LTS on .NET 10.
  An Umbraco upgrade moves a site from Umbraco 7, 8 or 13 to Umbraco 17 LTS on .NET 10. WebsiteSoft audits packages, custom code and integrations, migrates content, media and members, rebuilds custom editors for the new backoffice and adds redirects to protect rankings. The outcome is a supported, secure platform with easier future upgrades.
  - Q: How long does an Umbraco upgrade take? A: It depends on the starting version and the amount of custom code. A move from Umbraco 13 is usually shorter than one from Umbraco 7 or 8, where the backoffice, templates and packages typically all need rebuilding rather than updating.
  - Q: What happens to our content during the upgrade? A: Content, media and members are migrated into the new version and checked against the old site page by page. Nothing is retyped by editors. Where the content model changes, WebsiteSoft maps old properties to new ones and verifies the result.
  - Q: Do we have to upgrade before Umbraco 13 goes end of life? A: Umbraco 13 stops receiving security fixes on 14 December 2026, so a site left on it after that date carries growing risk. Planning the upgrade earlier in 2026 avoids a rushed project and leaves time for testing and cut-over.
